```{r setup}
library(simweightR)
```

# Introduction

The simweightR package is a lightweight R implementation of the data pre-processing pipeline described in [Buytenhuijs et al. (2024). "Differential T cell receptor gene expression analysis using the Wilcoxon test with similarity-based weighting"](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.03.28.645951v1).

The package pre-processes immunological sequencing data from T-cell receptor sequencing data by adjusting read counts based on the expression levels of highly similar TCRs. This improves true positive rates in differential abundance (DA) analysis.

# Data Input Format

simweightR expects a dataframe formatted according to [AIRR Standards 1.6](https://docs.airr-community.org/en/stable/datarep/rearrangements.html). The following columns are required:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `cdr3_aa` | Amino acid sequence of the CDR3 region |
| `consensus_count` | Read count for this sequence in this sample |
| `v_call` | V gene with allele (e.g. `TRBV12-3*01`) |
| `j_call` | J gene with allele (e.g. `TRBJ1-2*01`) |
| `sample_processing_id` | Sample identifier |

Other column names can be given with the arguments `cdr3`, `v`, `j`, `sample` and `count` of `simweight()`, e.g. `cdr3 = "junction_aa"` or `count = "duplicate_count"`.

The package includes a dataset from a mouse experiment, `mouse_pbs_srbc` (16,616 rows: TRBV2 sequences from the T cell zone of 4 control (PBS) and 4 immunized (SRBC) mice), and a small subset of it for quick testing, `mouse_pbs_srbc_mini` (71 rows):

```{r}
head(mouse_pbs_srbc_mini[, c("cdr3_aa", "consensus_count", "v_call", "j_call",
                             "sample_processing_id")])
```

```{r}
unique(mouse_pbs_srbc_mini$sample_processing_id)
```

# Running the Pipeline

## simweight()

The main entry point is `simweight()`. It validates the input, aggregates counts per sequence per sample, computes similarity matrices for sequences sharing the same CDR3 length and V-J gene pair, and returns the similarity-adjusted counts:

```{r}
x <- simweight(mouse_pbs_srbc_mini)
```

Key parameters:

- `method`: `"hamming"` (default), `"blosum"`, or custom function — see [Similarity Methods](#similarity-methods) below.
- `threshold`: similarity score threshold (default `0.8`) — see [Threshold Parameter](#threshold-parameter) below.

# Outputs

`simweight()` returns a list with three elements:

- `x$sequences`: one row per sequence, i.e. per unique combination of V gene, CDR3 and J gene, with columns `id` (e.g. `TRBV2_ASKEGPEVF_TRBJ1-1`), `cdr3_aa`, `v_call` and `j_call`
- `x$counts`: the original counts, one row per sequence (in the same order as `x$sequences`, with `id` as row names) and one column per sample; 0 where a sequence was not observed in a sample
- `x$weighted`: the similarity-adjusted counts, with the same rows and columns as `x$counts`

```{r}
head(x$sequences)
x$counts[1:4, 1:4]
x$weighted[1:4, 1:4]
```

A sequence keeps its original count if it has no neighbours above the similarity threshold. Otherwise its count is adjusted toward the weighted average of its neighbourhood.

The samples (columns) are in the order in which they first appear in the input. For DA analysis, take the sample labels from `colnames(x$weighted)`.

# Downstream Analysis

## Wilcoxon Test (via edgeR normalisation)

The following workflow normalises the count matrix with edgeR's TMM method and applies a Wilcoxon test per sequence. This is the approach described in the accompanying pre-print.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
x <- simweight(mouse_pbs_srbc)
count_matrix <- x$weighted

library(edgeR)

class(count_matrix) <- "numeric"
# condition of each sample, in the order of the columns of count_matrix
samples <- unique(mouse_pbs_srbc[, c("sample_processing_id", "treatment")])
condition <- factor(samples$treatment[match(colnames(count_matrix), samples$sample_processing_id)],
                    levels = c("PBS", "SRBC_4d"))

y <- DGEList(counts = count_matrix, group = condition)
y <- calcNormFactors(y, method = "TMM")
count_norm <- as.data.frame(cpm(y))

pvalues <- sapply(1:nrow(count_norm), function(i) {
  data <- cbind.data.frame(gene = as.numeric(t(count_norm[i, ])), condition)
  wilcox.test(gene ~ condition, data)$p.value
})
pvalues <- data.frame(pvalues, row.names = rownames(count_norm))
pvalues$fdr <- p.adjust(pvalues$pvalues, method = "fdr")

conditionsLevel <- levels(condition)
dataCon1 <- count_norm[, which(condition == conditionsLevel[1])]
dataCon2 <- count_norm[, which(condition == conditionsLevel[2])]
dataCon2 <- dataCon2[rownames(dataCon1), ]
pvalues <- pvalues[rownames(dataCon1), ]

foldChanges <- log2((rowMeans(dataCon2) + 1) / (rowMeans(dataCon1) + 1))
results_da <- data.frame(
  log2foldChange = foldChanges,
  pValues = pvalues$pvalues,
  FDR = pvalues$fdr,
  row.names = rownames(dataCon1)
)
results_da <- na.omit(results_da)
```

## DESeq2

DESeq2 requires integer counts. Round the weighted counts before passing them in:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
x <- simweight(mouse_pbs_srbc)
count_matrix <- x$weighted

library(DESeq2)

count_matrix_int <- round(count_matrix)
# condition of each sample, in the order of the columns of count_matrix
samples <- unique(mouse_pbs_srbc[, c("sample_processing_id", "treatment")])
col_data <- data.frame(
condition = factor(samples$treatment[match(colnames(count_matrix_int), samples$sample_processing_id)],
              levels = c("PBS", "SRBC_4d")),
  row.names = colnames(count_matrix_int)
)

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = count_matrix_int,
                              colData = col_data,
                              design = ~ condition)
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "SRBC_4d", "PBS"))
res_df <- as.data.frame(res[order(res$padj), ])
```

# Parameter Details

## Similarity Methods

The `method` parameter controls how sequence similarity is computed within each CDR3 length / V-J gene group.

**`"hamming"` (default):** normalised Hamming distance between equal-length CDR3 amino acid sequences. A similarity of 1 means the sequences are identical; each mismatched position reduces the score by `1 / length`. Fast and suitable for most use cases.

**`"blosum"`:** pairwise alignment scores using the BLOSUM62 substitution matrix, normalised to [0, 1]. Accounts for amino acid biochemical properties — conservative substitutions (e.g. Leu → Ile) receive a higher similarity than radical ones (e.g. Leu → Asp). More biologically informed than Hamming.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
x_hamming <- simweight(mouse_pbs_srbc_mini, method = "hamming")
x_blosum <- simweight(mouse_pbs_srbc_mini, method = "blosum", threshold = 0.9)
```

**Custom function:** you can also pass any function that takes a character vector of CDR3 sequences (all of the same length) and returns a square similarity matrix with values in [0, 1], in the same order, with 1 on the diagonal. The function is called once per CDR3 length / V-J group:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
my_sim <- function(sequences) {
  m <- matrix(0.9, nrow = length(sequences), ncol = length(sequences))
  diag(m) <- 1
  m
}
x_custom <- simweight(mouse_pbs_srbc_mini, method = my_sim)
```

## Threshold Parameter

The `threshold` parameter (default `0.8`) is the minimum similarity score for two sequences to be treated as neighbours. Sequences below this threshold do not affect each other's adjusted counts.

- A **higher** threshold (e.g. `0.9`) is more stringent: only nearly identical sequences are pooled together.
- A **lower** threshold (e.g. `0.7`) allows more distant sequences to contribute, increasing smoothing but risking blending of biologically distinct clonotypes.

```{r}
x_strict <- simweight(mouse_pbs_srbc_mini, threshold = 0.9)
x_lenient <- simweight(mouse_pbs_srbc_mini, threshold = 0.7)
```
